claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature mechanical loading.
Severe lattice distortion is the main cause of the claimed improvement in plastic strain and toughness.
The WTaTiVZr alloy possesses significant lattice distortion.
The synthesized WTaTiVZr alloy has a homogeneous high-entropy microstructure.
Commercially pure tungsten has a relatively uniform crystalline structure compared with the HEA.
Mechanical loading at 1200°C is representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service.
Temperatures at or above 1000°C are relevant to plasma-facing applications.
An inert or high-vacuum test environment avoids oxidation effects.
Lattice distortion and the resulting heterogeneous microstructure alter dislocation dynamics.
Lattice distortion and the resulting heterogeneous microstructure alter grain-boundary behavior.
Lattice-strain variations reduce dislocation pinning in WTaTiVZr.
Lattice-strain variations activate grain-boundary sliding in WTaTiVZr.
Reduced dislocation pinning and grain-boundary sliding promote dynamic recrystallization.
The combined dislocation, grain-boundary-sliding, and dynamic-recrystallization mechanisms improve elevated-temperature plasticity and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will have a lower yield point than pure tungsten.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will undergo more plastic deformation before failure than pure tungsten.
Loaded WTaTiVZr will exhibit refined grains and active grain-boundary sliding that are absent in pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten will exhibit higher yield strength, lower plastic-strain capacity, and lower toughness than WTaTiVZr under identical high-temperature conditions.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply at lower temperatures or when loading does not activate dynamic recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding.

contradictions.description: The initial state calls the HEA microstructure homogeneous, whereas the structural mediator calls it heterogeneous, without clarifying whether these refer to different scales or to chemical homogeneity versus strain or grain heterogeneity.
